canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/5. MST Problems/06. Number of islands 2.cpp

narrative.title: Live Landfall Counting on the Model Basin
narrative.scenario: A dredging simulator turns single sea cells into land one command at a time, and hydrology wants the live island count after every command — islands being land patches joined side-to-side. Each new cell either opens its own island or bridges up to four neighbouring islands into one, so a union-find ledger keeps the running tally without rescanning the basin.
narrative.inputFormat: Integers n, m (an n x m basin, initially all water) and a list operators of [row, col] landfall commands.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an array holding the number of islands after each operation.

testCases.explanation: The first two cells stack into one island; the two bottom-right cells form a second.
Re-filling an already-land cell changes nothing.

hintLevels: Level 1: Adding land can only merge islands or create one — never split them.
Level 2: Keep a live count: +1 when the cell is new land, minus one for each genuinely new neighbour merge.
Level 3: Flatten cell ids as row * m + col, guard double-fills, and snapshot the count after every command.
